_meta.description: Suggestion queue. Every item is a proposed change with its evidence, expected impact, effort, risk and dependencies. Nothing here is implemented until the owner (or a delegated reviewer) picks a path: accept, amend, or reject. Status values: proposed | recommended | accepted | rejected. This is the review surface the brief asked for: choose the best path before implementing.

statuses.proposed: Written and costed, waiting for a decision.
statuses.recommended: One correct path is identified in the recommendation line; still needs a nod.
statuses.accepted: The owner's standing brief mandated this item (or a reviewer accepted it). Implementation state is in the progress note.
statuses.rejected: Recorded as not adopted; revisit only if the recorded decision changes.

_meta.last_change: 2026-11-19 (arena/9f84489c-prod2): SG-03/04/06/09 moved to accepted/shipped with progress notes; SG-11..SG-17 added (design directions for the design prompt, decision-making improvements, measured topic selection, seasonal rotation, question pipeline, verification-angle growth).

suggestions.title: Adopt a consumer-facing brand name (after trademark clearance)
suggestions.problem: The wordmark 'Prod2' is the project's established name, not a shop name. A real brand name would help the site read as a publication and support a future domain.
suggestions.proposal: Shortlist 2-3 candidate names (e.g. 'Counter & Crisp', 'The Basket Guide', 'Crisp Ledger'), run each through a trademark search (Q-19), pick one, rename in one pass (masthead, titles, OG card), then consider a domain.
suggestions.evidence: D-18 kept the established name only because clearance (Q-19) was open; the constraint is clearance, not the name itself.
suggestions.impact: Medium — brand recall, SERP click-through, linkability.
suggestions.effort: One session once a name clears.
suggestions.risk: Trademark collision if skipped; mitigated by the clearance step.
suggestions.recommendation: Do it after clearance. Ranked 1 by impact/effort among brand items.

suggestions.title: Publish the comparison table's 'counter depth' as the lead spec
suggestions.problem: Capacity is what listings lead with, but counter depth is what buyers underestimate (the brief's counter-space thesis).
suggestions.proposal: Reorder comparison columns so counter depth and footprint lead; add a 'capacity per cm of depth' derived column with its formula shown (D-26 published the analysis; this makes it the headline).
suggestions.evidence: D-26 adopted the capacity-per-depth analysis; the counter-space guide is the site's most distinctive angle.
suggestions.impact: Medium — differentiation, matches the strongest guide.
suggestions.effort: Small (column reorder + one derived column in build).
suggestions.risk: Low. Derived values must show the formula to stay within the evidence rule.

suggestions.title: Build a seasonal thermometer cluster (grilling season, holiday gifts)
suggestions.problem: Half the catalog (P4/P5) has one guide only; seasonal demand for thermometers is a natural traffic window.
suggestions.proposal: Two question-shaped guides ('How accurate does a meat thermometer need to be?', 'Instant-read vs leave-in: which for which cook?') plus a gift-guide page, timed to seasons, each linked into sitemap + feed.
suggestions.evidence: The publishing-cadence requirement; the thermometer products' listing themes (grill/BBQ, stocking stuffers).
suggestions.impact: Medium-high organic potential; unmeasured until analytics exist (Q-P02).
suggestions.risk: Low — content only; no new claims needed beyond listed specs.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept after Q-P04, timed to season.
suggestions.progress: 2026-11-19 publication pass (owner brief mandated the seasonal rows): seasonal desks shipped in data/p2/calendar.json - Holiday hosting live with its own guide (guide-holiday-hosting.html), grilling season staged to open in May. The thermometer cluster is wired to its pillar page. The standalone gift-guide page stays optional.

suggestions.title: Reader email capture with consent flow
suggestions.problem: RSS is the only capture channel; a newsletter would build a returning audience.
suggestions.proposal: Add a signup form with reviewed consent + privacy text, kept clear of affiliate links (Participation Requirement 6(g)); double opt-in; no incentives tied to clicks.
suggestions.evidence: Q-47; FTC disclosure guidance travels with the channel (S-FTC1).
suggestions.impact: Medium — returning readers; but adds compliance surface.
suggestions.effort: Medium (form + consent text review + privacy note page).
suggestions.risk: Medium — privacy liability if consent text is wrong; gated on review.
suggestions.recommendation: Defer until traffic exists; the compliance cost is paid before any benefit arrives.
suggestions.progress: 2026-11-19 publication pass (brief mandated reader capture): the consent-gated "What should we answer next?" form ships on the front page and guides hub. It sends nothing until the consent basis (Q-47) is settled and a capture endpoint is configured (F-P07). Email capture itself remains gated behind that decision.

suggestions.title: Adopt a dated-snapshot price policy
suggestions.problem: Buyers want prices; the site withholds them (F-02) because they drift faster than re-verification.
suggestions.proposal: Publish price only with a mandatory read date + 'check listing' link; checks enforce price/date pairing; re-verify at each publishing pass. Ratings stay withheld (they invite selection bias).
suggestions.evidence: F-02; D-19 shows the dated-snapshot pattern already works for popularity claims.
suggestions.impact: Medium-high conversion relevance; adds upkeep to every pass.
suggestions.risk: Medium — stale prices damage trust more than absent prices; must be automated before adoption.
suggestions.recommendation: Only after the automated date-pairing check exists. Do not do this by hand.

suggestions.title: Deploy the analytics endpoint and turn on Search Console
suggestions.problem: No first-party measurement exists (F-19); topic selection is instinct instead of measured queries (Q-P02).
suggestions.proposal: Host analytics-endpoint/server.py on an owner-controlled HTTPS host; set settings.analytics_endpoint; verify the domain in Google Search Console; submit the sitemap; record weekly counts in the campaign ledger only from authorized reports.
suggestions.evidence: The brief's measurement-first priority; the machinery ships with this build.
suggestions.impact: High — everything downstream (topics, optimization, revenue reporting) depends on it.
suggestions.effort: Low-medium (hosting + config), mostly owner-side access work.
suggestions.risk: Low — the endpoint stores counts only, no visitor data.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept as the top operational priority. Nothing else compounds without it.
suggestions.progress: 2026-11-19 publication pass (brief mandated the Search Console row): readiness shipped - verification-token slot in settings.json, sitemap + robots + feed wired, step-by-step checklist on the measurement page. Property verification and endpoint hosting are owner actions (F-P06, F-19).

suggestions.title: Add a 'what it's like to live with' layer once real usage exists
suggestions.problem: S-06 (hands-on content) was recorded as not adopted because nobody has tested these appliances; listings can't tell a reader what cleanup or noise is like.
suggestions.proposal: Either (a) owner supplies first-hand notes/photos for one product and the site adds a clearly-labeled experience section, or (b) keep spec-only and say so. Do not fabricate experience.
suggestions.evidence: Google's thin-affiliation policy (S-GSPAM) rewards genuine experience; the current site is honest but thinner than ideal.
suggestions.risk: High if faked — never do this synthetically.
suggestions.recommendation: Option (a) if the owner can supply real notes; otherwise stay honest with (b). This is the single biggest content upgrade available.

suggestions.title: Sticky mobile comparison bar on product pages
suggestions.problem: Mobile readers scroll long comparisons and lose the buy path (S-20 in the brief list).
suggestions.proposal: A sticky bottom bar on the comparison and category pages showing the currently scrolled product + its sponsored link; type-scale and tap-target pass first.
suggestions.risk: Low — must keep disclosure visible and not obscure content (Participation Requirements on clarity).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept as a UX follow-up after the first traffic arrives.

suggestions.title: Internal-linking rule as an automated check
suggestions.problem: S-24's rule (every article reaches the comparison, the buying guide and its category pillar) is satisfied today by hand and can rot.
suggestions.proposal: Extend tools/checks.py: each guide must link to compare.html, buying-guide.html and its category page; fail the build otherwise.
suggestions.evidence: S-24/D-27 adopted the rule; automation is the brief's machinery-trust requirement.
suggestions.impact: Medium — keeps the site's structure intact as pages grow.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept. It is a gate, and gates are cheap once written.
suggestions.progress: 2026-11-19: implemented in tools/checks.py - every guide page must reach the comparison, the buying guide and its category pillar, and the gate fails the build when one is missing.

suggestions.title: Second-format expansion: one more air-fryer format page (basket accessories, liners, racks)
suggestions.problem: Adjacent accessory queries (liners, racks) are how many readers enter the category.
suggestions.proposal: A small accessories guide that links back to the three formats; only listed facts; no accessory products added to the affiliate set until their own intent records exist.
suggestions.evidence: Topic-hub structure of the publishing plan (S-13/D-17).
suggestions.recommendation: Defer until measured queries confirm demand (after SG-06).

suggestions.title: Design feed: three fully specified directions for the next visual pass
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for design suggestions that feed the design prompt, so a reviewer can pick the best path before anything is implemented. One direction (warm editorial) is carried and built; the alternatives have never been specified side by side.
suggestions.proposal: Publish three complete directions against the same compliance block: (A) Warm editorial - kitchen magazine that shows its sources: serif display (Fraunces), paper background, terracotta accent, drawn line-art only; this build follows it (DESIGN_PROMPT.md). (B) Clean modern shop - sans display (Inter), white cards, one strong accent color, product-first grid with big tap targets, tighter type scale; the most e-commerce-native of the three. (C) Bold magazine - high-contrast black/paper, oversized display numerals for specs, full-width section bands, editorial photography if the photography decision (Q-05/D-22 lineage, SG-18) ever clears. Each keeps: disclosure above the fold, no prices/ratings, sponsored-only product links, drawn-not-copied imagery.
suggestions.evidence: Owner brief 2026-11-19 (the site must look like a polished marketing affiliate publication, not generated output); carried D-18/DIR-A; DESIGN_PROMPT.md.
suggestions.impact: Decides the entire reader-facing look; direction B is the most shop-like, A is the most distinctive and least template-like, C is the boldest but needs photography.
suggestions.effort: The pick is one meeting; the token layer (SG-13) makes the implementation one session per direction.
suggestions.risk: Low if done through the token layer; high if done as scattered one-off CSS. Direction C depends on the photography decision.
suggestions.recommendation: Keep Direction A (already live, distinctive, cheapest to finish) unless the owner wants a more conventional shop look, in which case B. Decide at the same time as the brand name (SG-01) so the visual pass happens once.

suggestions.title: Decision-making improvements: dependency-ordered queue and the shortest credible path
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for suggestions on how to improve decision making. Decisions currently pile up in a flat log; blockers are visible only if the reader cross-references the questions register.
suggestions.proposal: Re-order the suggestion queue by dependency (what blocks what), give each open item a named decision-maker (owner / agent / data), and print a standing 'shortest credible path' block at the top: the smallest sequence of owner decisions that unblocks the most work. Also add a 'decide-by' date to items whose value decays (seasonal content, Search Console).
suggestions.evidence: Owner brief 2026-11-19; the questions register already maps what blocks what (Q-01 blocks S-08/earnings claims, Q-19 blocks the rename, Q-P02 blocks measured topics).
suggestions.impact: Cuts the owner's review time; nothing else changes reader-side.
suggestions.effort: One pass over the registers; the renders already exist.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept. Cheap, no downside, and it is exactly the review surface the brief asked for.

suggestions.title: Design token layer: color, type and spacing in one switchable place
suggestions.problem: The palette and type scale are hard-coded in assets/css/site.css. Switching a design direction (SG-11) today means editing declarations all over the sheet.
suggestions.proposal: Move the eight palette tokens, the two type stacks and the spacing scale into CSS custom properties at the top of the sheet; components consume only variables. Then a direction switch is a token-block swap.
suggestions.impact: Makes SG-11 reversible and the brand rename (SG-01) mechanical.
suggestions.effort: One session; visual output must be pixel-identical after the refactor (the build gate catches content changes, not pixels, so the pass includes a manual look).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept together with SG-11, whichever direction wins.

suggestions.title: Choose topics from measured queries after 14 days of real data
suggestions.problem: Topic selection is editorial instinct labeled as hypothesis (Q-P02). The brief wants the next topic chosen from measured queries instead.
suggestions.proposal: Once Search Console is verified (Q-P05) and the endpoint is hosted (F-19) and 14 days of data exist: pull the Search Queries report plus the endpoint's guide_read_75 counts, rank candidate questions by impressions and read-through, and let the top measured question set the next queue slot. Record the data date and the decision in the decision log; keep the ledger's rule (no revenue forecast).
suggestions.evidence: Owner brief 2026-11-19; measurement contract (data/p2/events.json); the campaign ledger's first-party rule.
suggestions.impact: Turns the queue from hypothesis to measurement; expected to change what gets written within two cadence cycles.
suggestions.effort: One review cycle per month after the gate opens.
suggestions.risk: Low - selection only, publication standards unchanged.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept. It is the payoff for SG-06 and requires no new machinery.

suggestions.title: Seasonal desk rotation as a standing module
suggestions.problem: The seasonal rows the brief mandates (nav labels, feed, Search Console, reader capture run in parallel with seasons and clusters) need a home that keeps rotating, not a one-off page.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the seasons list in data/p2/calendar.json as the source of truth; the front page renders the current season automatically from the calendar dates, and the guides hub groups by cluster and season. When a season ends, its module retires without a content edit - only the calendar changes.
suggestions.impact: Keeps the front page timely without rewrite churn; supports the holiday and grilling clusters already published.
suggestions.effort: Half a session to make the front page date-aware (currently the season modules are static blocks).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept before the next season boundary (2026-12-31).

suggestions.title: Question-to-guide pipeline from the reader-capture form
suggestions.problem: Reader questions arrive (once capture is connected) with no defined route into the publishing queue.
suggestions.proposal: When three or more captured questions share a theme, that theme earns a queue slot ahead of editorial hypotheses; the guide's 'what we could not verify' block cites the question IDs. Never publish the asker's words verbatim without consent.
suggestions.evidence: Q-47 (consent basis), Q-P02 (topic evidence), the brief's 'publish question-shaped guides, then measure whether anyone arrives'.
suggestions.impact: Closes the loop between readers and the queue; strong fit with the site's whole thesis.
suggestions.effort: A standing editorial rule once capture is live; no code.
suggestions.risk: Low, provided the consent text (Q-47) covers the use.
suggestions.recommendation: Accept in principle now; activate with the capture endpoint.

suggestions.title: Grow on the verification angle: the 'receipts visible' differentiator
suggestions.problem: The brief wants organic traffic from real buyers without volume tricks. The site's differentiator is not product coverage - it is that every figure shows its read date and source.
suggestions.proposal: Make the method the marketing: a short 'every number has a receipt' strip near the top of the front page (already shipped), cross-links from every fact table to the source register, and titles/meta that promise sourced specs rather than superlatives. Then measure (SG-14). No popularity claims, per D-19.
suggestions.evidence: Owner brief (the verification angle); Google Search Central helpful-content guidance (S-GHELP); D-19 evidence rule.
suggestions.impact: Positions the site against thin affiliate pages, which is the one advantage a small publication can actually hold.
suggestions.effort: Mostly shipped; remaining work is measured iteration (SG-14).
suggestions.risk: Low - the compliance block already forbids the alternative (hype).
suggestions.recommendation: Accept as the standing growth thesis.
